result.topic_en: Riemann sets up the variational problem for a minimal surface spanning a given contour, derives the first variation, expresses the Euler–Lagrange condition via normal angles r, φ, and introduces complex variables η = tan(r/2)e^{φi}, ξ = y+zi to express the differentials.
result.transcription:
Minimalfläche durch einen gegebenen Contour.
$M = \iint dy\,dz \sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2}$
$\delta M = \iint dy\,dz \frac{\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\frac{\partial \delta x}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}\frac{\partial \delta x}{\partial z}}{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}\right)^2}}$
oder, wenn
$-\cos r = \frac{\sin r\cos\varphi}{\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}} = \frac{\sin r \sin\varphi}{\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}\right)^2}}$
gesetzt wird,
$\delta M = \iint dy\,dz.\sin r\left(\cos\varphi\frac{\partial\delta x}{\partial y}+\sin\varphi\frac{\partial\delta x}{\partial z}\right)$
$= -\iint dy\,dz.\left\{\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(\sin r\cos\varphi)+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(\sin r\sin\varphi)\right\}\delta x$
Für das Minimum ist daher
$-\sin r\sin\varphi.dy+\sin r\cos\varphi.dz = d\zeta$
ein vollständiges Differential, und außerdem ist
$-tg\, r\cos\varphi.dy - tg\, r\sin\varphi.dz = dx$.
Man setze
$\eta = tg\frac{r}{2}.e^{\varphi i}$, $\eta' = tg\frac{r}{2}.e^{-\varphi i}$
$\xi = y+zi$, $\xi' = y-zi$
Hieraus folgt
$d\zeta = i\frac{\sin r}{2}(e^{\varphi i}d\xi' - e^{-\varphi i}d\xi) = i\frac{\eta d\xi'-\eta' d\xi}{1+\eta\eta'}$
$dx = -\frac{1}{2}tg\, r(e^{-\varphi i}d\xi + e^{\varphi i}d\xi') = -\frac{\eta d\xi'+\eta' d\xi}{1-\eta\eta'}$

methods.what: Area functional of a surface x(y,z) for the minimal surface problem
First variation of the area functional

methods.what: Parametrization of the surface normal by angles r, φ
methods.quote: $-\cos r = \frac{\sin r\cos\varphi}{\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}} = \frac{\sin r \sin\varphi}{\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial y}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\partial x}{\partial z}\right)^2}}$

methods.what: Integration by parts giving the Euler–Lagrange (zero mean curvature) condition in divergence form
methods.quote: $= -\iint dy\,dz.\left\{\frac{\partial}{\partial y}(\sin r\cos\varphi)+\frac{\partial}{\partial z}(\sin r\sin\varphi)\right\}\delta x$

methods.what: Minimality condition as exactness of a differential form defining a conjugate function ζ
Expression of dx in terms of the normal angles
Complex variables: stereographic-type normal coordinate η and complex coordinate ξ
Differentials dζ and dx expressed in η, ξ (Weierstrass-type representation)
